stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the core field of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The associated tags indicate its relevance within the transformers and safetensors ecosystem.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: More than 1 in 10 chance AI ‘could kill all humans,’ says Anthropic safety lead after colleague quits
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic safety lead warns of a >10% chance AI could cause human extinction by decade's end.
The warning follows a colleague's resignation due to concerns over uncontrolled 'superhuman systems' development.
The story highlights growing internal anxiety within leading AI labs regarding safety and rapid deployment.

stories.title: Drama swirls around OpenAI’s legendary mathematical milestone
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: OpenAI claims to have found a solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem.
This mathematical problem has been unsolved for approximately 90 years and relates to fluid dynamics.
The announcement was made via a blog post and has garnered significant media attention.

stories.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
stories.author: David Garcia
bullet_points: Observes emergent collective behavior in AI agents without explicit programming for cooperation.
Agents spontaneously utilized an external, un-designed resource (a public wiki) for mutual benefit.
The study provides a unique, observable record of agent interactions and environmental perception.

stories.title: Muse – Meta’s personal AI agent
stories.author: yks
bullet_points: Meta is developing 'Muse,' a personal AI agent.
This represents a significant move into personalized AI assistance from a major tech player.
The announcement signals Meta's continued heavy investment in advanced AI applications.

stories.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: a high-resolution map of human DNA
stories.author: utiiiD
bullet_points: DeepMind has released the AlphaGenome Atlas, a high-resolution map of human DNA.
The atlas is designed to be a predictive tool for understanding the impact of every possible DNA letter change.
This represents a significant advancement in genomic science leveraging advanced AI/ML capabilities.

stories.title: Gambling with our lives: AI researcher quits Anthropic with warning about safety
stories.author: taubek
bullet_points: An AI researcher has resigned from Anthropic, a major AI safety company.
The departure is accompanied by a warning regarding AI safety concerns.
This signals ongoing internal debates and potential risks within leading AI labs.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes key ML technologies such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key ML/AI tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking activity around a major LLM model.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed to run locally on user hardware for multi-step, context-aware tasks.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Speedups reach up to 90% when running coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI has introduced 'Sketch' within ChatGPT Images 2.5.
This new feature allows users to generate detailed AI images from simple hand-drawn doodles.
It represents an advancement in multimodal input for generative AI.

stories.title: Meta bets on AI agent Muse to catch up in AI race
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Meta is heavily investing in AI with the launch of Muse, a personal AI assistant.
Muse is positioned as a tool designed to make AI accessible to a broad user base.
This initiative is part of a larger, multi-billion dollar strategy to improve Meta's standing in the competitive AI landscape.

stories.title: Top chipmakers embrace ASML’s $400M machines, agree to crucial chipmaking change
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Major chipmakers are adopting new, high-value ASML lithography machines.
The industry has agreed to a crucial change in chip manufacturing processes.
This procedural shift is projected to increase the productivity of the new ASML equipment by 40%.

stories.title: “This is the AI men actually use”: Meta ads pushed apps nudifying real teens
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta is facing scrutiny for allowing ads that promote body image issues among young users on Instagram.
The issue involves targeted advertising nudging young girls toward 'nudifying' their photos.
The company was criticized for delaying the removal of these problematic advertisements.

stories.title: TANGO: Humanoid Navigation in Cluttered Environments with a Whole-Body Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Dhruv Shah
bullet_points: Introduces TANGO, a novel whole-body vision-language-action model for humanoid robot navigation.
Addresses the complexity of cluttered 3D environments, moving beyond traditional 2D path planning.
Focuses on continuous, geometry-aware whole-body adaptation, including gait and arm coordination.

stories.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in LLM agents: loss of procedural knowledge and objective tracking during long-horizon planning.
Introduces the 'Procedural Graph' as a novel execution structure to manage and constrain agent actions.
Aims to solve issues like out-of-order tool invocation and unproductive action repetition in complex agent workflows.

stories.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
stories.author: Sitaram Asur
bullet_points: The research proposes 'Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models,' suggesting that the surrounding system scaffolding (the 'harness') is as crucial as the model weights for agent success.
Automated harness evolution offers a path for smaller, cheaper models to achieve high performance on specialized tasks, mitigating the reliance on massive frontier models.
The study investigates the synergistic combination of harness evolution and lightweight fine-tuning across various enterprise agent tasks.

stories.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in LLM agents: the loss of procedural knowledge and objective tracking over long, complex execution trajectories.
Introduces the 'Procedural Graph' as a novel structure to explicitly manage the sequence, conditions, and flow of actions taken by LLM agents.
Aims to improve agent reliability by preventing out-of-order tool invocation and unproductive action repetition in long-horizon tasks.

stories.title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
stories.author: Ruihong Huang
bullet_points: Introduces SPINE, a new benchmark designed to test LLM robustness under sustained, adaptive disagreement.
Addresses the failure mode of 'sycophancy,' where LLMs abandon correct positions when challenged by users.
Evaluates production systems and LLM variants over up to 25 turns to capture emergent behavioral failures.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting Apple silicon hardware.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Apple’s foldable ‘iPhone Duo’ will reportedly start at $2,000
stories.author: Richard Lawler
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly developing a foldable phone, rumored to be named the 'iPhone Duo'.
The anticipated starting price for the iPhone Duo is suggested to be $2,000.
The report comes ahead of Apple's upcoming launch event, citing Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman.

stories.title: AI power users claim Anthropic duped them with subscriptions, and they’re taking it to court
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Anthropic is facing a class-action lawsuit from AI power users.
The core allegation is that Anthropic misled subscribers about the value of its top-tier pricing.
The dispute involves customer dissatisfaction despite Anthropic claiming power users are central to its business strategy.

stories.title: LG TV shown scanning LAN for third-party phones and other devices
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: LG TVs have been observed actively scanning local area networks (LANs).
The scanning appears to target third-party mobile phones and other connected devices.
The story touches upon the feasibility and implications of long-term data storage.

stories.title: NOAH: Learning the Full Patient Journey. A Longitudinal Multimodal Time-Aware Model for Representation and Forecasting
stories.author: Daniel Rueckert
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of fully exploiting vast, longitudinal, and multimodal patient records in healthcare.
The proposed NOAH model is designed to capture complex, irregular temporal dynamics and stochasticity in patient data.
It moves beyond current discriminative AI approaches to better represent and forecast patient state trajectories.

stories.title: A Data-Driven Framework for Identifying and Prioritizing RPA Opportunities in Healthcare Processes
stories.author: Juan Manuel Castillo
bullet_points: Addresses a critical industry problem: 30-50% of RPA initiatives in US hospitals underperform due to informal process selection.
Proposes a novel, data-driven, four-module framework to systematically identify, prioritize, and match RPA candidates.
The framework guides selection based on automation tier (e.g., Python bot, n8n, UiPath) and forecasts financial returns.

stories.title: ExecCritic: Learn to Test, Test to Improve for Coding Agents
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces ExecCritic, a new framework to improve coding agents by integrating test-verification and revision cycles.
Addresses the critical issue where agents can generate false confidence because their generated tests might not accurately reflect the required behavior.
Uses a role-specific reinforcement learning recipe within a test-verify-revise scaffold to guide agents toward correct repository repairs.

stories.title: DeCAL: Towards Physically-Grounded Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Models via Contact-Aware Latent Co-Imagination
stories.author: Shanghang Zhang
bullet_points: DeCAL addresses limitations in existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models when handling complex, contact-rich robotic manipulation.
The model specifically tackles challenges like visual occlusions and intricate contact dynamics inherent in dexterous tasks.
It introduces a novel approach that moves beyond homogeneous multimodal fusion by incorporating adaptive tactile integration and explicit physical dynamics modeling.

stories.title: MeClear: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Attribution and Risk-Aware Memory Clearance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
stories.author: Jun Zheng
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in long-horizon LLM agents: conventional memory retrieval prioritizes semantic similarity over actual downstream utility.
Introduces 'MeClear,' a new cooperative game-theoretic framework designed for task-conditioned memory clearance.
The framework actively identifies and removes memories that are outdated, misleading, or conflict with current task goals, improving agent reliability.

stories.title: Learning Length-Extrapolatable Recurrent Models
stories.author: Hanwen Jiang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of standard Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) in handling long-context dependencies due to BPTT failures.
Proposes that the failure of long-context learning is not solely due to gradient vanishing/exploding, but relates to 'state credit'.
Investigates how dense per-token losses can still enable training of shared recurrent rules despite severe gradient decay.

stories.title: NOAH: Learning the Full Patient Journey. A Longitudinal Multimodal Time-Aware Model for Representation and Forecasting
stories.author: Daniel Rueckert
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of exploiting vast, longitudinal, and multimodal patient records in digitized healthcare.
Proposes NOAH, a time-aware model designed to capture complex, irregular temporal dynamics in patient data.
Overcomes limitations of existing discriminative AI approaches by focusing on representation and forecasting patient state trajectories.

stories.title: When Does Scale-Invariant Optimization Become Unstable? An Exact Schedule Law with Weight Decay
stories.author: Rajiv Khanna
bullet_points: Investigates the stability boundaries of Scale-Invariant Optimization in neural networks.
Identifies a hidden feedback loop where learning-rate schedules and weight decay interact via parameter norm.
Proposes an exact discrete-time law governing this interaction, involving a self-quenching effect.

stories.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
stories.author: Kang Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SAEScientist-Bench, a framework to test AI agents' ability to conduct autonomous research on Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs).
Highlights the critical need for post-hoc monitoring and auditing (interpretability) to ensure safe alignment in AI systems, beyond just automated training.
Positions SAEs as a key mechanistic interpretability tool for isolating and understanding the features learned by complex models.

stories.title: ReCite: Agentic Reasoning for Faithful Citation
stories.author: Donghong Ji
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'ReCite,' an agentic reasoning framework designed to improve citation accuracy in academic writing.
Current automated citation systems, despite mitigating hallucination, still struggle with misattribution, even when citing real papers.
The research addresses the growing difficulty researchers face in manually navigating the massive volume of scientific literature.

stories.title: Studying Image Tokenizers as Visual Languages in Unified Multimodal Models
stories.author: Yang Liu
bullet_points: The research investigates image tokenizers as the 'visual language' within unified multimodal models.
It critiques existing evaluation methods for tokenizers, noting they often fail to capture joint behavior with text.
The authors introduce a controlled, pure-autoregressive testbed to track losses across multimodal tasks (T2I, I2T) during continual pretraining.

stories.title: ExecCritic: Learn to Test, Test to Improve for Coding Agents
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces ExecCritic, a new framework to improve coding agents by integrating test generation and execution feedback.
Addresses a critical flaw where agents can achieve false confidence by simultaneously generating faulty patches and tests.
Utilizes a test-verify-revise scaffold combined with role-specific reinforcement learning for agent training.

stories.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
stories.author: Kang Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SAEScientist-Bench, a framework to test if AI agents can autonomously conduct research using Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs).
Highlights the critical need for post-hoc monitoring and auditing in AI development to ensure safe alignment and understand model learning.
Positions Mechanistic Interpretability tools, specifically SAEs, as essential for bridging the gap between automated training and verifiable model understanding.

stories.title: Most 'AI Agents' Are Just If-Statements in a Trench Coat
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article critiques the current state of 'AI Agents,' suggesting many are overly complex facades.
The author argues that many existing agents are functionally limited, often resembling simple conditional logic ('if-statements').
It highlights a gap between the perceived sophistication of AI agents (planners, tools) and their actual underlying capability.

stories.title: Why I built a zero-telemetry Chrome extension to measure the physical cost of AI prompts
stories.author: ib2mofficial
bullet_points: The article discusses the growing reliance of developers on Large Language Models (LLMs).
The author built a zero-telemetry Chrome extension to track the physical cost associated with AI prompts.
This addresses the often-unseen environmental or operational costs of using LLMs in development workflows.

stories.title: I let a model suggest Postgres indexes, then made the database mark its work
stories.author: remdore
bullet_points: A tool was developed to automate the process of testing LLM-suggested PostgreSQL indexes.
The tool validates suggestions by creating them in a transaction, re-measuring performance, and checking planner usage.
The experiment showed that approximately 60% of the LLM's index suggestions were ineffective.
